utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, everyone. I would like to ask the registrar to be kind enough to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Case Number IT-96-23/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the record, could we have the appearances of the parties, please. For the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney. At my side, Ms. Djurdja Mirkovic, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am attorney Milenko Radovic from Foca or Srbinje, representing the accused Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I wish to ask Mr. Stankovic whether he can follow the proceedings in a language he understands.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am getting the French interpretation, so I was not able to follow. Which channel should I switch to? [In English] Six? [Interpretation] I am not getting the interpretation. I am getting French on channel six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call a technician to fix this, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am getting it now. I am hearing you now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Stankovic, are you hearing me now in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. It is my understanding that there was a meeting between the parties within the framework of Rule 65 ter, when the parties confirmed that the obligations stemming from Rule 68 are being implemented and that there are no complaints in that connection. Unless I hear the opposite from either party, then I assume that that is the case. I think we should now move on to another topic which has to do with a motion that Mr. Stankovic has filed with the registry a few days ago. As the rules require that the motions need to be drafted in one of the official languages of the Tribunal, the translation has still not been completed and therefore I have not been able to familiarise myself fully as to what it is about. But I understand that in general terms in this document Mr. Stankovic is endeavouring to develop his views with regard to his defence. Without entering into any detail regarding the content of a document which I have not had a chance to study in detail, it is in a sense my duty in order for justice to be served to advise Mr. Stankovic to organise and coordinate his views and defence strategy with his counsel. And that way, one can be sure that the same defence strategy is applied that fully corresponds to the interests of Mr. Stankovic. Having said that, I should also like to state that we believe that the pre-trial stage has been completed and that it is now up to me to prepare the report as required by the -- of the Pre-Trial Judge by the rules and to submit it to the President of the Chamber so that we can move on to the next stage, the second stage, of the proceedings. And as I hear no opposite views I assume that the parties are in agreement that the pre-trial stage is indeed -- has indeed been completed and that the case is ready to be transferred to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When it comes to finalisation of this proceeding, indeed I would like to put forward a question to you. When Your Honour confirmed that there has been a kind of motion and this motion referred to some defence, should it be my conclusion that this is a motion towards the Registrar that isn't included in the proceedings so far in an official way? Because I haven't seen such a kind of motion and I can hardly accept that whenever such a motion is filed to the Registrar without being -- without any notification to the Prosecution team, that we as a Prosecution team should be able at least to consider the content of it. Now, to -- in sum, my question is: The motion you referred to from Mr. Stankovic, is it part of the filed -- of the filings in this proceeding or should it be considered as a separate filing on the own responsibility of Mr. Stankovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. That is a highly relevant question, but to the best of my knowledge this is a kind of declaration by Mr. Stankovic in which he clearly explains that he is not responsible of any of the crimes that he is accused of. Therefore, I believe that this, in a sense, strengthens the motion already filed by the Defence and in response to the pre-trial brief of the Prosecutor. So I don't see that that can change in any way the position of the Prosecutor, who has said what she thinks. And it is now up to the Defence to express itself. The Defence counsel has filed a brief and quite recently, if I'm not mistaken, I think it was the 28th of June, that this filing was sent to the Registry. So this is a statement by Mr. Stankovic, whereby he reiterates his position in principle and that is to say that he is -- was not involved in the events of which he is accused. I am telling you this even though until now I have not been able to have a complete insight into the contents of that statement, but through a nonofficial translation which was provided to me, I believe that it contains the same position that Mr. Stankovic upheld from the very beginning and it goes along the same lines as already indicated by the Defence counsel. So if you find nevertheless that before we can state that this pre-trial stage has been completed, if you need to have time to make any remarks or observations - however you can always do that - and should your observations be of such a nature as to require a revision of the decision closing the pre-trial stage, then my position could be reviewed on the basis of your own submissions or observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I -- to a minimum, I would like to see the content. Because we are discussing something now that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And a second issue is that -- the issue of the alibi defence, and I would further on have a -- would like to present a submission for that, because before finalising this stage I would like to refer to Rule 67 with a view to further explain the witnesses and the concrete evidence referred to in the pre-trial brief with a view to alibi. But please give me your opinion with a view to give the Prosecution team the time to translate this motion, to consider whether or not this is a motion because it was not filed in a copy towards us, and we have to see what's in it. It might be also a kind of alibi defence, and then we have to further go and follow a proceeding according to Rule 67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to meet the requirements of the parties and also the interests of justice, I will wait before drafting my report for a certain period of time once this statement has been registered - and I will call it a statement - so you will have an opportunity to make your submissions or observations that you may have and I will give them my full attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, thank you. And then if you -- would you allow me, please, to make the submission according to Rule --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. According to Rule 67, it should be that whenever the Defence intends to offer an alibi defence that there should be a specification of the place or places at which the accused claims to have been present at the time of the alleged crime, and the names and addresses of witnesses, and any other evidence upon which the accused intend to rely to establish this alibi. We already put Defence counsel on notice of that obligation whenever it had been initially raised that in a letter of the 16th of September, 2003, but that was a kind of initial consideration by the Defence. And then we immediately as a kind of response confirmed to the Defence counsel, please be aware of the obligation of Rule 67(A)(i). When I reviewed to that extent the pre-trial brief by the Defence, I noticed that in paragraphs 63 and 68, together with paragraph 173, explicitly evidence had been offered not being in Miljevina in period August-November 1992 and that the exact time periods will be provided when it comes to those places, including Foca. So explicitly offers done for evidence -- through this evidence it can be established and in various paragraphs in addition every time reiterated that its evidence is available after investigation by the Defence, meaning that now has the time come that the pre-trial Judge is able to set a time limit according to Rule 67 to provide the Prosecution, and of course the pre-trial Judge, with this specific information as envisaged in Rule 67. Now I would like to draw your attention to this specific rule and the interest of the Prosecution to take a look at this information, because it might as well be a support of the fact finding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I believe that what you are saying is based on the wording of Rule 67(A)(i), and perhaps that is the reason why I advised Mr. Stankovic to coordinate with his counsel when preparing what I call the defence strategy. However, you're raising a point which is very valid and I'm referring to the letter of the rule and I quote in English: "The Defence shall notify the Prosecutor of its intent to offer." Therefore, the word is "shall," which means that it is an obligation. It is not optional. And in that connection, I would like to hear the Defence counsel, what he intends to say in paragraph 63, 68, and 173 of his pre-trial brief and also has he familiarised himself with the content of what Mr. Stankovic has filed and what his opinion is with regard to the implementation of Rule 67(i). So I would like to hear the Defence counsel now please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, Mr. El Mahdi, may I be given a minute to say something with respect to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give you the floor, however we're talking about a point of law, now. So I would prefer to hear your counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I wanted to say was that it is my pre-trial brief and my response to all the paragraphs of the pre-trial brief submitted by the Prosecution. That's what I wanted to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But it hasn't been translated yet, so the parties are not abreast of the contents of the document. And there's a point of law that we've come to now which we're discussing. It is a point of law which consists of the following on the basis of the clear letter of the rule of Rule 67 which states that: "If an accused wishes to defend himself with the defence of alibi, he must notify the -- the Defence shall notify," is the exact wording, "shall notify the Prosecution of its intent to offer by a deadline stipulated by the Trial Chamber or the pre-trial Judge." So it is on this point of law that the Prosecution has now raised an issue, a point of law in fact, and it is on this matter that I would like to hear your Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, I do apologise, Mr. El Mahdi, if the Defence gives a precise alibi, that is to say, the time period incorporated by the alibi, then this gives the Prosecution a chance of moving their assertions outside that time period and outside the alibi itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Will you listen to me. We're not going to invent things here. I would like you to follow the proceedings, to follow what I'm saying, and to follow the reading of the rule itself. And the rule specifies, and I quote: [In English]: "The defence of alibi; in which case the notification shall specify the place or places at which the accused claims to have been present at the time of the alleged crime and the names and addresses of witnesses and any other evidence upon which the accused intends to rely to establish the alibi." [Interpretation] So I understand your concern. You're saying that if you reveal all this information then the opposite side is going to make use of that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's precisely it. They're not going to claim that something happened on the 5th of August, for example, but they're moving the date to the 10th of August, for instance. So I'm giving an example, a hypothetical, which means that if I state the time relevant to the alibi and if I give the precise date, then that means that this gives the Prosecution the opportunity of changing its claims outside that time frame and not to say that something happened, say, on the 1st, but to move it on and say it happened on the 15th. Do you understand me? I'm not a lawyer, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic, just a moment. Would you wait a moment, please. If I give you the floor, if I give you an opportunity to express yourself, that does not mean that you can use every opportunity to speak. Everybody here in the courtroom must abide by the strict rules of the Tribunal, and they can be summarised in a word and it is the Judge who decides on the procedure to be followed. So you have expressed your point of view, we have heard you out. I would now like to ask you to be quite certain of one thing and that is that first of all, I'm going to ask your counsel to present his views on this point of law that we're discussing. So I'm not going to ask him to address the facts. It is a point of law. The Prosecution raised a point of law and it is now up to your Defence counsel to respond to that point of law. He's not going to disclose anything, any information that you don't want him to disclose.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I apologise Judge El Mahdi. I do apologise. It was not my intention to irritate you. I wanted to present my views. All I wanted to do is say what I thought. I didn't mean to irritate you at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That will do. Let us hear Mr. Radovic now. Counsel Radovic has the floor now on this point of law we have been discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I come to the point of law we're discussing, I would just like to say a few words with respect to the pre-trial brief which I submitted as the lead counsel on behalf of Mr. Radovan Stankovic. The brief, or rather, pre-trial brief was compiled by me and written out by me with full acquiescence from Mr. Stankovic. With respect to all the observations set out in the brief, there was full agreement between myself and Mr. Stankovic. Having received the go-ahead from Mr. Stankovic for me to compile the pre-trial brief, I filed the pre-trial brief, I handed it over to the Court, in fact. It is Mr. Stankovic's discretionary right -- and there are no restrictions on him being able to present his own views in the matter and especially with respect to some questions that he considers to be vital for him personally and were not dealt with and elaborated in my pre-trial brief. I have told Mr. Stankovic that I have to write the brief, to compile the brief, on the basis of Rule 65 ter (F), and that is what I did indeed do. And that is why I would like to say that the brief was compiled with full agreement reached between myself and Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something at this point? I would like to congratulate you for the cooperation that there has been between Mr. Stankovic and yourself. However, my question now is: Can we take it -- are we to understand that your brief which refers to a defence of alibi, is that what it does? Because the Prosecution made specific reference to paragraph 63, 68, and 173, which leaves some doubt as to whether you are indeed going to raise the defence of alibi. So the Prosecution is quite clear. They say if the Defence raises the defence of alibi, then this comes under Rule 67 and they have the obligation to convey all the information mentioned in the rule. So my question is: In your brief did you have and do you have the intention of resorting to the defence of alibi? Is that what you're going to do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true that the Defence previously in one of its written motions and indeed at the last Status Conference and in its pre-trial brief did mention that the defence of Mr. Stankovic would also rest on a defence of alibi. The Defence is still working on the evidence, and at all events it will, in a timely fashion through its preliminary brief and in conformity with Rule 67(A)(i), inform the Prosecution and Chamber thereof so that our colleagues of the Prosecution and their investigators will certainly be able to, if they so desire, and before the witnesses are heard before the Trial Chamber, talk to them. The Defence will certainly file the written motion before the deadline stipulated by Rule 65 ter (G) when it will finally give the witnesses to testify to the alibi and state the exact locations at which Mr. Stankovic was during the time when the alleged crimes were committed, which he has been accused of and other evidence in proof will also be presented, upon which the Defence is going to rest its defence case as the defence of alibi. The Defence did not wish to file the brief before its pre-trial brief was sent in. That was one reason. And also because of the processing of this case, bringing it to court in Bosnia-Herzegovina, where according to the laws of the land in force at present there is no obligation of a defence -- no obligation on the part of the Defence to present to the Court evidence and proof of a defence of alibi. Finally, Your Honour, if you order, or rather, decide and rule today that the Defence is duty-bound to present and file the brief within the deadline given, the Defence will, as has been the case so far, abide by your ruling and fulfill its obligation. With respect to evidence and proof of the defence of alibi, I have talked to Mr. Stankovic. However, with respect to all this evidence and the time period and time frame concerned as well as the names of the witnesses, we have not reached a final agreement in that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, counsel. I see that there is a question of law which merits reflection, and that is to know whether paragraph (G) of Rule 65 ter allows the Defence not to reveal the information related to the defence of alibi, because alibi -- the alibi you say is linked to the testimony of witnesses which -- and you're afraid that the witnesses might change their testimony or point of view. So it is because of the very nature, if I understand you correctly, of the defence case resting on the defence of alibi which is fundamentally based on the testimony of witnesses, and you're saying in fact that in that specific instance the application of Rule 67 must bear in mind and take into account what was said -- what is in fact stated in Rule 65 ter paragraph (G). At all events I invite the parties to communicate their point of view with respect to this issue, and I think that there is no deadline, no specific deadline for that to take place. Let's say a month and a half, two months for you to have enough time to clearly state your point of view on this point of law without going into the details of course, but to address this point of law specifying the specific nature of the situation in this case and that the alibi is linked to the testimony of witnesses and that you are afraid that the witnesses themselves, if their names are known, might be upset, or rather, that the proceedings might suffer if the names were known in advance. So I am going to give you until the end of August. Does that suit you, counsel? Is the end of August sufficient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you're going to set a deadline, as I said a moment ago, I am -- and I am discussing the defence of alibi with Mr. Stankovic, then this will be based on witness testimonies. We have selected a list of witnesses and the events that these witnesses are going to testify about. Now, in view of the fact that you're giving me a deadline today within which I have to file my brief linked to the allegations of a defence of alibi, I should like to ask you to enable me to have sufficient contact with Mr. Stankovic and to hear his ideas and his presentation of the case so that I could present it in the brief, that you give me until the end of September if you would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So I'm going to give you all the time you need to reflect upon the matter, to discuss it with Mr. Stankovic. I'm not going to set a limit or deadline. I'm not going to set a date as a deadline. I'm going to give you a free reign, enough time to think about the matter and consult Mr. Stankovic for as much as you need because it is a question that deserves a lot of thought. But I would like to ask you to focus and concentrate on how you're going to coordinate the provisions of Rule 67 with Rule 65 ter paragraph (G) to marry the two in this particular case. Having said that, I think that this answers the queries of the Prosecution and concerns. We're going to leave the question open. We're going to give the Defence every possibility of thinking about the matter, and then presenting their views to the Chamber and to myself and that will of course be conveyed to the Prosecution. In the meantime if the Prosecution is going to have all knowledge of the filings of Mr. Stankovic's brief, he has asked to be able to file them until the 28th of June -- they were filed on the 28th of June, in fact. And now this brings me to the last question, which is to inform -- to see about Mr. Stankovic's health. So I'm going to ask Mr. Stankovic what his health situation is like and would he prefer that we go into private session for him to be able to give us an update? If he wishes to raise any matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no need, Mr. El Mahdi. With respect to my health it would be better for you not to ask me anything. How can my health be after all these false accusations and threats that have been made, threats by the Prosecution, rulings that are not in conformity with the law and everything else that you are doing to me against the law and you're not allowing me to take the floor and speak myself? So I should like to ask you to give me 15 minutes to be able to state my views clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic, I think that with full appreciation of your desire to express yourself and to speak, and it is precisely why I asked you about this and made myself acquainted with the document that you redacted, however unfortunately it was not registered. So I don't think that you can say that I am not sensitive to your situation. It is I who am speaking and when I speak please listen to me. Therefore, as I was saying, I am very much aware of your situation and sensitive to it. And I think that everyone has made a great effort to bring things out into the open and make things as clear as possible. So I think that you had ample opportunity to express yourself through a document even more than the rules stipulate for, the Tribunal's interior rules. I think your document was 146 pages long, unless I am much mistaken. So you did indeed have ample opportunity to present your views as far as I know and you let them be known to the Chamber and to one and all. So I don't understand how it is that you say that I'm not giving you the opportunity to present your views. And let me remind you of something else. Throughout the last audience, the last proceedings and Status Conference that we held, I gave you the opportunity of speaking. You took the floor, but I also said -- I said to you: Mr. Stankovic, this isn't the right time, the proper time, to go into the basics of your defence case. It is a Status Conference, a preparatory stage leading up to the trial, and it -- the affair will of course be tried before the Trial Chamber when the time comes. Perhaps I wasn't being clear enough, but I did give you at least 15, if not 20 minutes, to take the floor. You availed yourself of that opportunity and you spoke about the substance and basics. I told you that that was not the time or the place to do that. Of course I understand that you wish to assert and confirm and reiterate your own positions, namely that you say again that you're innocent. I do understand your position and I think that you indicated this feeling to us very well through the document that you filed with the registrar. Therefore, I do not see how it is that you can say that I don't give you the opportunity of expressing yourself. You know to express yourself need not be orally during the proceedings. You can also express yourself to your counsel, and he will compile a brief and you yourself wrote a document. And so I'm sure that in both these instances you set out your thoughts fully. So all I'm asking you to do now, in view of these circumstances - and I sympathise with your situation and circumstances being in detention - if you're suffering from any disorders or anything like that, perhaps I can help you to alleviate your suffering in any way, if you are indeed suffering. So that is all I wanted to ask you. And if I understand you correctly, you just said that you are not complaining of anything specific, except the general situation that you find yourself in, that is to say in detention. And I can sympathise with that fully. Having said that, would any of the parties like to add anything else? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. I would please raise four issues. The first issue is the label of the personal statement given by the accused. It had been qualified by the accused himself as a pre-trial brief. It had been confirmed by you as a pre-trial Judge that he has the right to file his personal view, but in addition --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting. I didn't qualify the document; I just said that he filed a statement, which you can qualify as a statement. Therefore, when not really going into the substance of that document, I'm fully aware of your concern and I specified that it was a document submitted by the accused. So I think we can agree on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. That means for me that I will not label this as the official -- the statement by the -- this document referred to by the accused as the official pre-trial brief as 65 ter under (F).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was described as a document filed by Mr. Stankovic, and the Defence counsel took the position that he filed his pre-trial brief. So one can assume that we have the pre-trial brief, the one submitted by the defence counsel for Mr. Stankovic and that Mr. Stankovic himself filed a statement. One can call it a statement; he expressed his views.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this confirmation. The second issue is the document itself, the number of pages: If I recall, it's around 140 pages. If that's correct and if it is indeed in B/C/S, that means a problem for both Chambers and Prosecution and also yourself, Your Honour, whenever you want to read this document to the full extent, as it is not in another language of the Tribunal. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Allow me to respond immediately. Mr. Stankovic wanted to express himself and when he expresses himself he may be repetitive occasionally. I cannot impose on him the rule that one imposes on counsel, a jurist who knows full well how to summarise his thoughts. But someone else who is not, by training, a jurist, for him it is very difficult to express his views in summary form. Therefore, it is in accordance with the very substance of justice to allow Mr. Stankovic to express himself even if he goes beyond certain quantitative limits in terms of pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you for that. My question -- the question -- the request I would put forward is that: With the backlog of translation facilities by CLSS, it is of importance as we are not now in trial, so we have no trial priority, that I request to you the support by you to translate this on short term in English in such a way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me answer immediately. It has been taken up by the translation section, which will probably finalise the translation today. So you may have it even today or maybe tomorrow in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The third out of four issues is that I really regret, Your Honour, that there is no deadline for the request done by me -- put forward by me within the framework of Rule 67. The deadline has officially gone but might be taken and interpreted by you as a request by Defence counsel for a new deadline. Within your discretion, and of course I respect it, you prefer not to give a deadline and to give the full possibility in time to prepare by Defence counsel. That also means that we might end up somewhere in October or November or December whenever filings are not according to speed pre-trial. And I regret that in advance because, well, I would like to support at least a speeding up in such a way that you grant -- if you prefer an extended time, but at least set some time limit at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would again like to respond immediately to this point. Not to impose a limit means that the limit is 120 days, in fact, because if one follows the rules - and we have to follow the rules - we need to meet for another Status Conference within 120 days at a maximum. And I think that it is quite in order to allow the Defence to, in consultation with Mr. Stankovic, to file a clear position within that time period. I should also like to point out that I am fully aware and willing to grant a reasonable time period -- maybe not reasonable, but reasonable for you. You will mean one thing but reasonable in a neutral sense, reasonable that is in accordance with the Defence strategy. It is not quite clear that one can lay down once and for all the strategy that will be pursued. And we must give the Defence time to prepare, to consult, to elaborate its own position regarding this subject. And I would also like to indicate that, a priori, we need to get to the bottom of things. In explaining Rule 67(ii) [as interpreted] in the light of what is said in Rule 65 ter, especially regarding the testimony of witnesses. It must be said that I expect the Defence to express its views regarding this point of law. And if the Defence is not obliged to convey to its list of witnesses except at the end of this stage, there could be an argument of law which I would like to hear from both parties, primarily the Defence but also from you, to see whether this is a witness that I am going to call in the Defence case or would I be obliged from the very outset to reveal the witness's name to the Prosecution. This could lend itself for reflection at least. And it is with regard to this point of law that I've asked the Defence to submit a filing to us on that point. In response to what you said, I indicated a time period that does not exceed 120 days, number one. And number two, this is something that reconciles the strategy on the one hand and the requirements imposed by Rule 67 but read in the light of Rule 65 ter. I think that it is quite in order to say in summary that the Defence has 120 days on the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Last issue. It's more a confirmation from my side. I was -- I noticed that Defence counsel was confirming a kind of argumentation with a view to his strategies that there is a court proceeding for a kind of referral of the case. Well, officially, from my point of view there is no decision in that regard made by neither the Trial Chamber or by Prosecutor or whoever in that regard. So that's totally new for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the extent to which nothing has been decided - and one cannot speculate - it is not a question for speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. El Mahdi, I would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will give you the floor. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. First of all, I wish to say that my filing consists of 73 pages and not 149. It consists of 149 paragraphs and it contains that many paragraphs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute, please. Wait a minute. We've resolved that. We can't allow unnecessary debates.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you can't. I'm not a lawyer, that is true. But I'm not so ignorant as to have to repeat myself a hundred times. As you said a moment ago, I was repetitive occasionally because the Prosecution in its brief is constantly repetitious in the belief that a lie repeated 100 times become the truth. Just look at their pre-trial brief and you'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you cut off the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So many indictments have been changed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Defence counsel, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to refer to a point made by the Prosecution that the Defence has exceeded the time limit for submitting notification of defence of alibi. If I interpret correctly Rule 67(A) what it explicitly says is it is the duty of the Defence to notify the Prosecution of its intent to offer the defence of alibi but certainly before the beginning of trial. The trial has not yet been scheduled. Rule 67 doesn't say how many days before the beginning of trial it is our duty to submit this notification. Since I have said that Mr. Stankovic's defence will be based on statements of witnesses when it comes to the alibi and in view of the fact that Rule 65 ter (G), as I have already said, says that we are obliged to provide a list of witnesses that the defence intends to call before the beginning of the defence case. So we haven't failed in any respect with regard to the time limits. As lead counsel, I will fully abide by your ruling and will submit my submissions after consultation with Mr. Stankovic within the deadlines you have set. And with regard to Mr. Stankovic's statement, I have said that it is his discretionary right to file such a statement, because the rules of procedure do not impose any such restrictions on him as would prevent him from doing so. And finally, I wish to say that in our view the pre-trial stage has been completed and the Defence is quite ready for trial, or rather, for the pre-trial conference, which we feel should be scheduled as soon as possible. The more so as Mr. Stankovic has been held in the Detention Unit for a whole of two years now, and sending him or referring him to a court in Bosnia and Herzegovina would certainly further prolong his detention which would undermine the fairness of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question of referring the case I don't think is a question to be discussed, because in my opinion this is a matter that is quite unknown to me. I need to specify, however, that what we need from you during the time ahead is a response to what the Prosecution has raised. They are saying that as soon as you declare your intention to offer a defence of alibi, you have to fulfill the conditions specified in Rule 67. What I am suggesting to you is that you respond to this argument within a time limit that you may choose. If I have given you up to 120 days, it doesn't mean necessarily that you have to wait for 120 days. You can file it tomorrow, a note saying and specifying your point of view. So it is in your interest that I didn't impose on you any deadline. Finally, before we adjourn this Status Conference I think we can say that we are waiting for the Defence to file a submission regarding the point raised by the Prosecution with respect to the obligation of the Defence to provide the information clearly indicated in Rule 67. Finally, Mr. Stankovic, I give you the floor now. Quietly and slowly and calmly, please, so that I can follow what you're saying. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wish to inform you of the illegal decisions made by the Tribunal's registry. You would not allow me to speak about it last time and you asked my attorney, Mr. Radovic, whether he was unable to have any contact with his client. Let me tell you: It wasn't that he was prohibited from contacting me, but I was prohibited from contacting him. So I had a prohibition on contacting my lawyer, my family, and my consulate. There were dual decisions; one said that -- the illegal one, and which says a prohibition on contact with all persons, including attorney. Please don't interrupt me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic, wait. You have to hear what I'm saying after all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you gave me the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait. Mr. Stankovic, I cannot allow such behaviour. I'm telling you once and for all: I give you an opportunity to speak which means that you, too, have to respect the rules that I am imposing. I am telling you that all the measures that you were referring to were passed on to the competent authorities, the President of the Tribunal, and it is not within the competence of this Chamber. And I quite understand and I am au courant with your requests.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no one else to complain to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand you're complaining against the decisions taken by the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They're illegal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic -- From the Prosecution, do you have any observations to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cut off the microphone for the accused, please. Do you have anything to add, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour. It is my observation that the pre-trial phase has not finalised, pending this information provided by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that that is quite clear. And with that, the hearing is adjourned. Thank you. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 4.18 p.m.
